extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and counsel handling USPTO reciprocal-discipline matters
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for imposing reciprocal discipline on a practitioner before the USPTO pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 (discipline predicated on state disciplinary action), including notice, opportunity to respond, sanction imposition, publication, and reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline predicate (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed where a practitioner 'has been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a State,' predicating a USPTO disciplinary action on the state discipline (here cited as violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may impose discipline based on a state's ethical discipline; the Final Order states the Respondent's reciprocal discipline is 'predicated on his violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), having been disciplined by a duly constituted authority of a state.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (37 C.F.R. § 11.24 procedure)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must send a 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' to the respondent and provide an opportunity to file a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline within forty (40) days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order was sent by certified mail and 'provided Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline ... based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).' Compliance with the notice and time frame is required for the respondent to raise defenses under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) no genuine issue)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the Office may determine there is 'no genuine issue of material fact' under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and proceed to impose reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, because Respondent 'received the Notice and Order ... but has not filed a response,' the OED determined no genuine issue of material fact existed and that suspension was appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imposition of identical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline imposed by the USPTO is to be identical to the discipline imposed by the disciplining state authority (e.g., same suspension duration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Complaint requested that the USPTO 'impose reciprocal discipline upon Respondent identical to the discipline imposed by the Presiding Disciplinary Judge of the Supreme Court of Arizona'; the Final Order suspends Respondent for two (2) years, consistent with the Arizona order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for action (35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO takes disciplinary action pursuant to federal statute and USPTO regulation (here cited as 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Suspension states: 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.' These provisions provide the legal basis for imposing and publishing discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and commencement of suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order specifies the suspension duration and that it 'commences on the date of this Final Order.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent 'is suspended ... for two (2) years, commencing on the date of this Final Order.' The order also clarifies continued suspension until reinstatement per applicable rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement petition requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner remains suspended until the OED Director grants a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'Respondent shall remain suspended ... until the OED Director grants a petition requesting Respondent's reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.' Practitioners must follow § 11.60 for reinstatement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice of Suspension in the Official Gazette describing the respondent, registration number, suspension period, and the rule violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs publication and provides sample notice language: it identifies the respondent, registration number, suspension length, violation (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)), and the underlying state rule violations (Arizona Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5 and 8.1 and Rule 54(d)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to disciplinary agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in states where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifically orders that notice be given to state disciplinary agencies and courts where Respondent is admitted as required by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties of disciplined practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 11.58)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as a condition of discipline (e.g., duties typical of disciplined practitioners such as client notice and case transitions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states: 'Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58;' practitioners should consult § 11.58 for the full list of post-discipline obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and electronic accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the respondent's name from any Customer Number(s) and USPTO verified Electronic System account(s), if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires the USPTO to dissociate Respondent's name from Customer Numbers and verified electronic system accounts to effectuate the practical consequences of suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions are made available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (URL provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes that disciplinary decisions are available at https://foiadocuments.uspto.gov/oed/ and directs publication and public notice consistent with transparency obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: State disciplinary findings as supporting facts (state rule violations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The factual and legal basis for USPTO reciprocal discipline may rely on the state tribunal's findings (e.g., violations of state rules of professional conduct such as practicing while suspended and failing to respond to lawful demands).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Suspension recounts the Arizona action: suspended for violating Arizona Rules of Professional Conduct 5.5 and 8.1, and Rule 54(d), 'predicated on practicing law while suspended and failing to respond to a lawful demand for information from the Arizona Bar.' Such state findings are incorporated as the predicate for USPTO discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Complaint and request for identical discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director initiates reciprocal-discipline proceedings by filing a 'Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' requesting imposition of discipline identical to the state-imposed discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The procedural step is described: the OED Director filed a Complaint requesting reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the state presiding disciplinary judge.
